items.stem: In an SN2 reaction, how does the nucleophile approach the electrophilic carbon?

options.text: From the side opposite the leaving group, causing inversion of configuration
options.rationale: Correct: backside attack gives the characteristic inversion.

options.text: From the same side as the leaving group, with retention
options.rationale: That describes neither SN2 geometry nor its stereochemical outcome.
That is SN1, not the concerted SN2 pathway.

options.text: Only after the leaving group has fully departed
options.rationale: SN2 is concerted; bond making and breaking are simultaneous.

items.explanation: Correct: backside attack gives the characteristic inversion.

items.stem: Which TWO features increase the rate of electrophilic aromatic substitution? (Select TWO.)

options.text: An electron-donating activating substituent on the ring
options.rationale: Correct: activating groups raise electron density and speed substitution.

options.text: A substituent that stabilises the arenium-ion intermediate
options.rationale: Correct: stabilising the intermediate lowers the activation barrier.
Nitro groups deactivate the ring and slow substitution.

options.text: Removing all substituents to leave benzene
options.rationale: Benzene is the unactivated baseline, not faster.

items.explanation: Correct: activating groups raise electron density and speed substitution.

items.stem: Why must an AI-proposed retrosynthetic step be checked before use?

options.text: Suggested reagents or conditions may be infeasible or unselective in practice
options.rationale: Correct: predictions need experimental and expert feasibility checks.

options.text: Retrosynthesis tools cannot propose any valid steps
options.rationale: They often propose valid steps; verification is still needed.

options.text: Every proposed step is guaranteed to work
options.rationale: No such guarantee exists for predicted chemistry.

options.text: Checking is only needed for inorganic reactions

items.explanation: Correct: predictions need experimental and expert feasibility checks.
